Senses.Explanation: A public address or instruction to the assembled community, and a recurring discourse heading rather than a private exchange. Across 12,002 occurrences in 399 allowlisted texts, records mark it with “addressing the assembly, saying” (示眾云/曰), sometimes after ascending the seat, and place it beside the formal hall address (上堂) and small convocation (小參). Yuejiang Zhengyin compares the small convocation with the address to the assembly; Ruibai Mingxue also delivers one in writing after the assembly answers a question. The format includes final instructions (臨終示眾), as when Luopu Yuanan begins by asking the assembly about one matter. Chan thus turns “show to the assembly” into the institutional name of a public verbal address.
Senses.Note: Primary Zen-institutional sense. Split from physically displaying an object. The formal hall address (上堂) and small convocation (小參) remain neighboring format entries. Written-verse instruction belongs here because the verse addresses the assembly; it does not create a third sense merely by changing medium.

Occurrences.Kwic: 陞座示眾云。鉤頭有餌。句裏無私。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄), second hall-address section. Yuanwu Keqin mounts the seat and addresses the assembly; the complete unit then records his exchange with a monk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂示眾，不立別名者，俱借五參一事統攝。

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The governing subject is the editorial rules section itself: the sentence classifies unseparated headings for hall addresses and assembly addresses under the five-day convocation. It is not presented as a person's speech turn or action.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Essentials from the Patriarchs' Addresses (列祖提綱錄), editorial rules: the narrative editorial classification places hall addresses and assembly addresses without separate names under the five-day convocation. The grammar presents a source-level genre rule, not a personal speech turn.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Essentials from the Patriarchs' Addresses (列祖提綱錄), quoted Huangbo address. The line explicitly names Huangbo Xiyun as the speaker; the surrounding compiler and later commentator do not own his exact turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 夜來撾鼓升堂，喚作小參；今日陞堂撾鼓，謂之示眾。示眾、小參，初無二說；夜來、今日，豈有兩般？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuejiang Zhengyin (月江正印禪師語錄), second Dianshan section. Yuejiang Zhengyin compares the previous night's small convocation with today's address to the assembly; the complete address stays in his voice.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Abridgment of Chan Master Guting's Sayings (古庭禪師語錄輯略), verse-commentary section quoting Luopu's final encounter. The inline marker names Luopu Yuanan as the speaker who opens the final address and questions the assembly.

Occurrences.Kwic: 尊者從三昧起。示眾曰。我所得法。而非有故。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of Five Lamps (五燈會元), section on the seventh patriarch Vasumitra. Vasumitra rises and addresses the assembly in the stored line; the section boundary and preceding life account exclude the neighboring patriarchs.

Occurrences.Kwic: 因中也設問，眾荅之，不愜師意，故書偈示眾曰：秪因日起明中暗
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Ruibai Mingxue (入就瑞白禪師語錄), verse on the intent of addressing the assembly. The title and author line identify Ruibai Mingxue as the teacher who writes the verse after the assembly's replies fail to accord.

Senses.Explanation: A physical display in which an object is shown or raised before the assembly, distinct from delivering a verbal address. The Zen Buddha holds up a flower while everyone remains silent (拈花示眾). Yuanwu Keqin raises a whisk, Yaoshan Weiyan a donated pair of trousers, and Yangshan Huiji a mirror, then questions the assembly. The flower defines the Zen Buddha through the flower-sermon deployment, while the whisk shows the teaching-seat implement in use without assigning it an unattested meaning.
Senses.Note: Different physical objects instantiate one display action; they are not separate senses. Split from spoken instruction because displaying an object and delivering an address are different acts.

Occurrences.Kwic: 世尊在靈山會上，拈花示眾，眾皆默然
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Joint Lamp Compendium (聯燈會要), section on Shakyamuni Buddha. The complete flower encounter names Shakyamuni as the actor who holds up a flower before the assembly; Mahakasyapa smiles afterward.

Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄), first hall-address section. Yuanwu Keqin raises the whisk, displays it to the assembly, and asks whether they see; the full unit then continues in Yuanwu's voice.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有施主施裩。藥山提起示眾曰。法身還具四大也無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of Five Lamps (五燈會元), embedded Yaoshan case within the Mengxi section. The line explicitly names Yaoshan Weiyan as the actor who raises a donated pair of trousers and questions the assembly; Mengxi speaks only after this old case.
